title: The Insurers Deciding if Hormuz Is Safe
gist: An FP Live event page previewing a discussion with Marsh CEO John Doyle on how insurers are pricing the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz risk, noting that tanker transit premiums through Hormuz have jumped 10 to 40 times higher than pre-war levels since the conflict broke out in February, with Marsh in direct talks with U.S. officials on restoring Gulf maritime trade.

themes.theme: Insurance pricing as a real-time conflict-cost gauge

insights.claim: Since the Iran war broke out in February, premiums for tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz have jumped from 10 to 40 times higher than before the war, illustrating how insurance markets price conflict cost even before broader economic effects become visible.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: A 10x-to-40x tanker insurance premium spike is a directly quantifiable, tradeable proxy for Gulf shipping risk and a leading indicator embedded in freight and energy-logistics costs — relevant for oil-tanker shipping economics and downstream fuel-price forecasting tied to the Hormuz conflict.

insights.claim: Marsh, the world's largest insurance broker, has been in direct talks with U.S. officials on restoring Gulf maritime trade, with CEO John Doyle set to discuss how insurers price conflict, geopolitical risk, and natural disasters more broadly.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Marsh's direct engagement with U.S. officials on Gulf trade restoration signals that private insurance-market normalization is being treated as a policy lever for de-escalation — worth tracking Marsh/insurer commentary as an early signal of any Hormuz risk-premium reduction.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'John Doyle is the president and CEO of Marsh'

insights.claim: The article frames insurance pricing as a general-purpose gauge of conflict cost: without viable insurance, economic activity of all sorts plummets, whether in conflict zones or areas prone to wildfires, floods, or earthquakes.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: A useful general framework — insurance availability/pricing as the binding constraint on economic activity in risk zones — applicable beyond Hormuz to any conflict or disaster-exposed asset class an investor is evaluating.
insights.quote: If you want to measure exactly how costly a conflict can be, ask the insurers.
